1#main: A firstborn of an impure animal—in what, in whom, and in what place it applies, and likewise its redemption and breaking of the neck. In it are 23 seifim. A firstborn of an impure animal applies in every place and at every time; and it applies only to donkeys. And this is its mitzvah: every Israelite who has a donkey that gave birth for the first time redeems it with a sheep—from sheep or goats, whether male or female, whether unblemished or blemished, whether large or small—and gives it to the kohen. And from when is he obligated to redeem it? From birth until death; but it is a mitzvah to redeem it immediately so as not to delay the mitzvah. And after he redeems it, it is entirely non-sacred and permitted in shearing and work like other non-sacred animals; and the kohen does with the sheep as with other non-sacred animals.
2#main: They do not redeem with a calf, nor with a wild animal, nor with a slaughtered sheep, nor with a treifah, nor with kilayim, nor with a koy.
3#main: They do not redeem with a sheep that resembles another species; and if he redeemed, it is redeemed. (And some say if he redeemed with it, it is doubtful (Tur in the name of the Rosh).)
4#main: They redeem with a "son of a breech birth." (And some say they do not redeem with a son of a breech birth (likewise in his name).)
5#main: If he has no sheep to redeem it, he redeems it for its value (and then he may redeem with any item (Beit Yosef in the name of the Rambam)) and gives its value to the kohen. Torah did not speak to be stringent upon him but to be lenient—for if he had a firstborn donkey worth ten selaim, he may redeem it with a sheep worth a dinar. In what case is this said? When the value of a firstborn donkey was three zuz and upward; but if its value was less than three zuz, they do not redeem it except with a sheep or three zuz. A generous eye does not reduce below a sela; a stingy eye—half a sela; average—three zuz. {Rama: And they redeem with one sheep many times—such as if he bought it back from the kohen, or in a place where he has doubt of a firstborn donkey whose law is that he separates a lamb for it and it is his (Tur).}
6#main: Immediately when he separated the lamb for a firstborn donkey, the firstborn donkey returned to non-sacred status—even before he gave it to the kohen, and it is permitted to benefit from it. And if it died, it is not buried, and the kohen acquires the sheep immediately; and it is on the owner's liability—if it died in the owners' hands before they gave it to the kohen, they are exempt. Therefore immediately when he separates it, he blesses "Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning redemption of a firstborn donkey."
7#main: An Israelite who redeemed his fellow's firstborn donkey—it is redeemed, and the firstborn donkey belongs to its owner.
8#main: A firstborn donkey is forbidden in benefit until it is redeemed; and if he sold it before redemption, its money is forbidden. {Rama: And specifically if he sold it without specification; but if he informed the buyer that it is a firstborn donkey and he sells him what it is worth beyond the sheep with which he redeems it, the money is permitted—even l'chatchila it is permitted to sell it in this manner (as implied in Tur).} And if it died before redemption, or they broke its neck—it is buried, because it is forbidden in benefit; even after breaking its neck, since it was not redeemed. Therefore if he did not redeem it and gave the firstborn donkey itself to the kohen, it is forbidden for the kohen to use it until he redeems it with a sheep and takes the sheep for himself, or breaks its neck and buries it. And kohanim are suspected regarding this matter; therefore it is forbidden for an Israelite to give a firstborn donkey to a kohen unless he redeems the donkey in his presence or breaks its neck in his presence.
9#main: A firstborn donkey before it is redeemed—it is forbidden to work with it and to shear it in order to benefit from its wool; but if its wool was tangled or it has a wound in the place of the wool, it is permitted to shear it for its benefit; and the wool is forbidden in benefit and is buried.
10#main: An Israelite who has doubt of a firstborn donkey separates a lamb for it to nullify its prohibition and keeps the lamb for himself. {Rama: If he did not wish to redeem it nor give it to the kohen, he strikes it on the neck with a hatchet until it dies and buries it (Tur).}
11#main: A firstborn donkey—they do not kill it with a stick, reed, sickle, saw, or axe—only with a hatchet; and one does not put it in a room and lock it until it dies, as it says "and you shall break its neck."
12#main: The mitzvah of redemption precedes the mitzvah of breaking the neck.
13#main: A donkey that had not previously given birth and bore two males—he gives one lamb to the kohen. Male and female—doubt; and he separates one lamb to nullify sanctity from it until it is permitted in benefit, lest the male was born first; and this lamb he separated is for the owners and not for the kohen, for the burden of proof is on the one who extracts from his fellow.
14#main: Two donkeys that had not previously given birth and bore two males—he gives two lambs to the kohen. Male and female—the male is for the kohen. Two males and a female—one for the kohen, and on the second he separates one lamb and it is for himself. Two males and two females, or two females and a male—there is nothing for the kohen. (And some say he must separate and they are for himself (Tur).)
15#main: One had previously given birth and one had not, and they bore two males—he gives one lamb to the kohen. Male and female—he separates a lamb and it is for himself.
16#main: One who buys a donkey from a gentile and it is unknown whether it previously gave birth and bore a male—he redeems it with a sheep and it is for the owners, because it is doubtful.
17#main: An Israelite who inherited from his mother's father a kohen—a definite firstborn donkey; and that kohen inherited from his mother's father an Israelite—he separates a lamb and it is his.
18#main: A convert whose donkey previously gave birth—doubt whether before he converted or afterward—he separates a lamb for it and it is his.
19#main: Kohanim and Levites are exempt from a firstborn of an impure animal. (And the same applies to a kohenet and leviah; but their husbands are obligated in their firstborn donkey. But in her melog property they are exempt, for she has partnership in it (responsum of the Rashba siman 366).)
20#main: Partnership with a gentile releases in it; and all laws of partnership with a gentile in a pure animal apply likewise in an impure animal—except that it is forbidden to partner with him in order to nullify its sanctity, since redemption or breaking the neck is possible.
21#main: Partnership with a kohen or Levi releases in it.
22#main: A gentile who separated a firstborn donkey—they inform him that he is not obligated, and behold it is permitted in shearing and work.
23#main: A cow that bore in the form of a donkey, and a donkey that bore in the form of a cow—was explained in siman 315.
